metaDescription: Six pole saws at or under $300, from Greenworks 60V and 80V cordless models to a RYOBI ONE+ bare tool and a 48cc gas saw, compared on power and ownership.
expertTake: The Greenworks 60V 10-inch is the best overall buy for a cordless saw that can handle serious limbs, since it arrives with a battery and charger on a brushless high-voltage platform. The DOWILIN gas saw is the budget route to maximum cutting capacity. Anyone with a few small branches a year should not spend at this level.
introParagraphs: Near the top of the consumer pole saw range, the questions change from reach and weight to torque and platform. Higher-voltage battery systems and gas engines are what let a pole saw finish a thick limb without stalling.

The decision is which power system you want to live with for years, and whether the box contains everything you need. Prices move, and the $300 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 10-Inch Brushless Cordless Pole Saw 2.0Ah
products.description:
The 60V platform is why this saw belongs in a different class from the 20V kits. Electrical power is volts times amps, so a 60V pack delivers the same watts at a third of the current, which keeps the brushless motor cooler and holds chain speed when the bar is buried in wood. A 10-inch bar then gives it the capacity for thick limbs.

The 2.0Ah pack is small in amp hours, but at 60V it stores much more energy than 2.0Ah at 20V, which is why you should compare watt hours, not amp hours alone. It comes with a charger, so the box is complete. Compared with the 80V Greenworks, you give up some top-end power and gain a kit that works out of the box.

Ownership is easier than gas: no mixing fuel, no carburetor and no pull cord. Store the pack indoors and keep the chain oiled. It is the right choice for a homeowner with mature trees. Expect to feel the benefit of the high voltage most when the bar is buried in a limb thicker than your wrist, where lower-voltage saws slow down and smoke the chain. Rest between long cuts so the motor and pack can cool.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with mature trees who want cordless torque.
pros: Sixty-volt brushless system holds chain speed

products.name: Greenworks 80V 10-Inch Cordless Pole Saw Tool Only

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Tool only, no battery or charger

products.description:
The 80V version is the highest-voltage saw in the group, sold as a bare tool. Higher voltage means more sustained power at lower current, so it keeps its speed in thick wood better than the 60V sibling.

Because there is no battery or charger in the box, the real cost depends on whether you already own 80V Greenworks gear. If you do, it is an excellent add-on. If you do not, the pack and charger make it an expensive entry.

Store the battery indoors and keep the chain oiled. Because the box has no battery, check that your pack matches the platform voltage and that the charger is the right model before you buy. A spare pack from another tool in the same family will run it. Some owners buy this to pair with an 80V mower or trimmer, which makes the bare-tool price an easy decision. If you do not own the battery, treat the real price as tool plus pack plus charger.

products.name: RYOBI P4360 18V ONE+ 8-Inch Cordless Pole Saw Bare Tool
products.description:
The RYOBI P4360 runs on the ONE+ system, one of the largest battery families in home tools. An 8-inch bar covers typical limbs and the bare-tool price is low if you already own ONE+ packs.

It is an 18V tool, so it lacks the torque of the 60V and 80V saws. Treat it as a tool for ordinary pruning.

Check whether you need a battery and charger. Do not overlook the ONE+ battery you may already own, because the cheapest way to start is with a pack from your drill. Keep the head clean and the chain oiled. Because it shares a battery with other ONE+ tools, the lowest-cost route is often borrowing the pack from your drill. Do not forget that lower voltage means slower cutting in thick wood.
products.bestFor: ONE+ owners with ordinary pruning needs.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Pole Saw 14 ft with 4.0Ah Battery
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN is a complete 20V-class kit with an 8-inch bar, a 4.0Ah battery and charger and a claim of up to 325 cuts per charge. It is the lower-voltage, lower-cost option in this list.

Its power is adequate for typical suburban limbs but will bog down on thick wood.

Keep the chain oiled and the battery indoors. Compare the full setup cost with the Greenworks 60V kit before deciding, because the gap between a branded kit and the cheapest bare tool is often small. Check the angled head locks firmly. The angled head and the claimed cut count make it a sensible choice for moderate limbs, and the 4.0Ah pack gives it more stamina than the smaller Greenworks cell. Add a spare chain to the shopping list.

products.name: DOWILIN 48cc Gas Pole Saw 11.5-Inch Bar
products.badge: Best for Thick Limbs on a Budget
products.description:
The DOWILIN gas saw has an 11.5-inch bar and a 48cc two-stroke engine, the largest bar in the group. Gas delivers torque without a voltage limit.

It needs mixed fuel, a clean air filter and a spark plug, and it is heavier and louder than the cordless saws.

Drain or stabilize fuel for storage. Follow the fuel mix on the label and run the engine until it uses up the fuel before storage. Ear protection is not optional with a two-stroke over your head. It is the only option here that does not depend on a battery system, which can be a relief if you have no existing tools. Keep a fuel can, bar oil and a spare spark plug on a shelf.
products.bestFor: Thick limbs without buying into a battery system.

products.name: YardenX 2-in-1 Cordless Pole Saw and Mini Chainsaw 8-Inch 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
The YardenX is the budget import in this list, a 2-in-1 with two 4Ah packs and a handheld mode.

It cannot match the 60V and 80V saws for torque.

Keep the chain oiled. Treat the claimed reach as a ceiling, and test the pole lock before lifting. The handheld mode is useful for low branches and brush. Because the pack count is two, rotating them evenly extends the life of both. The 2-in-1 design lets you remove the pole and use the head as a handheld saw for low branches and brush, which adds value for a small yard.
products.bestFor: Light pruning with a handheld mode.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Greenworks 80V and 60V saws deliver sustained power at low current, so they keep chain speed in thick wood. The RYOBI 18V, CRAFTSMAN V20 and YardenX 20V saws bog down sooner. For limbs near the bar length, voltage matters more than anything else. Weigh the saw with a battery attached, since the head weight is what you feel overhead.
A 2.0Ah pack at 60V stores more energy than a 4.0Ah pack at 20V. Compare volts times amp hours when you compare kits. Ask whether replacement chains for your bar size are sold locally.

The DOWILIN gas saw has the longest bar and no battery limit but needs fuel mixing and engine upkeep. A 60V or 80V cordless saw is quieter and simpler. Choose gas only if you will maintain it. A fiberglass pole is lighter than metal and safer around wires, but neither should go near power lines.

The Greenworks 80V and RYOBI P4360 are sold without a battery or charger, while the Greenworks 60V and CRAFTSMAN include them. A high-voltage battery can cost as much as the saw. If you only prune a few small branches a year, a higher-voltage saw is a luxury.

A 10 or 11.5 inch bar cuts thicker limbs than 8 inch. Rough capacity is half the bar length. Do not buy a longer bar than you can hold overhead. Think about storage: a gas saw needs a place away from heat and flames.
Wear a hard hat, eye and hearing protection, stand outside the drop zone and never use a metal pole near power lines. Check that the oil reservoir has a window so you can see the level.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power system
howWeEvaluated.description: We graded voltage and engine size. The Greenworks 80V and 60V and the gas saw led. Voltage and engine size decided the order for thick limbs, while convenience decided it for light pruning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether batteries and chargers ship. The Greenworks 60V and CRAFTSMAN scored well. Kit contents were compared by battery capacity and charger inclusion.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting hardware
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bar length and motor type. Maintenance needs, such as fuel mixing or battery storage, counted as part of ownership.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed fuel, battery and parts needs over several seasons. Reach and wattage claims were discounted when they could not be checked.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept guidance conservative. Owner feedback patterns informed the durability view. We kept safety guidance conservative, since a pole saw drops limbs from above.

cards.text: The 60V saw ships with a battery and charger and has enough torque for most mature-tree limbs.

cards.label: 80V
cards.text: The 80V saw has the most sustained power but is sold as a bare tool, so it makes sense only for 80V owners.

howToChoose.note: Pick 60V for a complete kit; pick 80V only if you already own the batteries.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A longer bar, high voltage or gas, and a sharp chain. A limb should be thinner than half the bar length.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 60V and the DOWILIN gas saw are the best fits.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have large limbs near or above the bar length, or want professional-grade durability. Those needs call for an arborist or a larger saw.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You prune small branches. A CRAFTSMAN or RYOBI covers it.

maintenance.why: A dry chain overheats and dulls. Check the spark plug and air filter at the start of each season on the gas saw, and clean sap off the bar.

maintenance.task: Mix fuel correctly or stabilize it
maintenance.why: Wrong ratio or stale fuel causes hard starts on gas saws. Keep the pole sections clean and dry so the locks grip.
A slipping lock is a hazard overhead.
Cold or heat accelerates fade. Wipe sap off the bar with a rag and solvent made for the job, and check the oiler window before each session.

faq.a: For limbs up to about half the bar length, yes. Beyond that, hire an arborist. Rest the pole on a strap when you can.

faq.q: Why is the Greenworks 80V cheaper but harder to buy into?
faq.a: It is a bare tool. You need an 80V battery and charger, which can cost as much as the saw. Wire the check of box contents into your buying routine.

faq.q: Is gas still better for thick limbs?
faq.a: It has the longest bar and no battery limit, but it needs fuel and upkeep. Gas saws need proper fuel mixing, so read the manual first.

faq.q: Can I use these in the rain?
faq.a: Electric saws should stay dry. Gas saws handle damp work better. Never use a metal pole near wires.

faq.q: What safety gear do I need?
faq.a: A hard hat, eye and ear protection, and a clear drop zone. Never use a metal pole near power lines. Wear sturdy boots. Use the three-cut method on heavy limbs, and keep your body clear of the line of fall.
